title: The Lord in every heart
hook: ghatt ghatt mai har joo basai: the Lord dwells in every heart, as the holy proclaim (Salok M9, ang 1427)

segments.voice: Yesterday, meraa: none of it goes; what we call mine is lent. So what is truly near? Today's salok answers.

Sikh tradition tells of a man named Bhai Ghanaiya. During the battles around Anandpur, he carried a water skin across the battlefield and gave water to the wounded, to Sikhs and to the soldiers they were fighting. Some Sikhs were furious and brought him before Guru Gobind Singh. The Guru asked him why he was helping the enemy. Bhai Ghanaiya is remembered as answering that he saw no enemy: in every face, he saw only the Guru. The Guru, the story says, gave him ointment as well, and told him to bandage their wounds too.
screen: `BHAI GHANAIYA'S WATER SKIN.` → `WATER FOR BOTH SIDES.` → `IN EVERY FACE, THE GURU.`

segments.voice: His answer echoes today's salok, written by Guru Gobind Singh's own father. Ghatt ghatt mai har joo basai, santan kahio pukaar. In paraphrase: the Lord dwells in every heart; the holy ones have proclaimed it aloud. Then: says Nanak, meditate on Him, O mind, and you'll cross the terrifying ocean. Ghatt means a clay pot, a vessel, and from that, the body or heart that holds a life. Ghatt ghatt: pot after pot, every single vessel. Not just the devout or the kind, or our own people. Every vessel. And pukaar is a loud call, a shout: the holy haven't whispered this. Last week, in the forest hymn, the Lord was within like scent in a flower; that was about finding God inside yourself. This salok turns the same teaching outward. Every vessel means mine, and yours, and the stranger's, and the soldier's on the other side. That's what makes it hard. Seeing God in the people we love comes more easily. The salok doesn't stop there. Sikhs see the same line at work in langar, which feeds anyone who walks in, of any faith or none, seated together on the floor. Seva, service, isn't reserved for members either. And Bhai Ghanaiya's water skin is what the line looks like when someone lives it.
screen: `GHATT GHATT: EVERY VESSEL.` · `PUKAAR: THE HOLY CALL IT ALOUD.` · `TURNED OUTWARD: THE STRANGER TOO.` · `LANGAR FEEDS ANYONE.` · then, large: `IN EVERY HEART.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person you find difficult, not your worst enemy, just someone who annoys you or whom you've written off, and picture the salok's clay vessel. You don't have to like them; let the thought sit, the Lord dwells here too, and notice what softens and what resists. If you pray, you can hold them before Waheguru for one breath.
Ghatt, a vessel, the heart. Ghatt ghatt mai har joo basai: the salok says the Lord lives in every ghatt, every heart, as the holy proclaim aloud.
Your line: in every heart. Every heart includes the ones on the other side. That's day five hundred ninety-two.

screen: `DAY 592 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: UNTOUCHED BY PAIN AND PLEASURE.`

howItsDone: Sikhs serve langar to anyone who comes, seated together on the floor, and remember Bhai Ghanaiya, who gave water to the wounded on both sides, as a model of seeing the Lord in every heart.

original.note: Gurmukhi: ghatt, a clay pot, a vessel, and so the body or heart. Ghatt ghatt: in every one.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Lord in every heart is a nice thought about inner peace.
what it means: it turns outward: the same Lord lives in the stranger and the opponent, so they are owed care too.
what a scholar hears: ghatt, a clay water pot, is an old Indian image for the body as a vessel holding a life, and Gurbani uses it constantly for the heart where the Lord is found.

chat.says: Why did Bhai Ghanaiya give water to the enemy soldiers too?
options: He saw the Guru in every face; the Lord dwells in every heart, even the enemy's.
He didn't know which side they were on, so he helped everyone by mistake.
He was secretly working for the other side, and the Guru forgave him for it.
chat.meaning: Ghatt ghatt mai har joo basai: the Lord lives in every vessel. Every heart means every heart, the stranger's and the enemy's too.
